newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India defers closing of diesel, kero term tenders.
newsitem.headline: India defers closing of diesel, kero term tenders.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has decided to defer the closing date of its four annual term tenders to buy high speed diesel and superior kerosene for June 1997-May 1998 deliveries, traders said on Tuesday.
The tenders will now close on May 7, instead of April 29, while the validity will now be until May 11 instead of May 3, they said.
The first tender seeks 12 cargoes of 40,000-to-45,000-tonnes each of 0.25 percent sulphur diesel for delivery to Kandla on the Indian west coast.
The second tender seeks 12 cargoes of 40,000-to-45,000-tonnes each of 1.0-percent sulphur diesel for delivery to Kandla and to Madras, Haldia, or Vizag on the east coast.
The third seeks 12 cargoes each of 87,000 tonnes and/or 130,000 tonnes of 1.0-percent sulphur diesel for delivery to Kandla.
Deliveries have to be between 1-7 and/or 16-23 of each month, on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis.
The kerosene term tender seeks 40,000-to-45,000-tonne cargoes for delivery to Madras or Haldia, and 30,000-tonne cargoes for delivery to Bombay on the west coast, c-and-f basis.
Last month IOC declined to accept any offers for its initial term tender to buy diesel and kerosene.
